title: Direct, inverse and linear relationships
blurb: Read slope as a rate and the intercept as a starting value, and tell direct, inverse and linear relationships apart from an equation, a table or a graph.
question: A wheelchair van charges C = 2.5m + 35 dollars for a trip of m miles. What do the 2.5 and the 35 mean, is the cost directly proportional to the miles, and what would an 18-mile trip cost?

teach.h: Three ways two variables can move together
teach.body: Formally, a linear relationship has the form y = mx + b, with a constant rate of change m (the slope) and a starting value b (the y-intercept). Direct variation, y = kx, is the linear case with b = 0. Inverse variation, y = k/x, keeps the product xy constant. In plain English: linear means 'start somewhere, then add the same amount each step'; direct means 'double one, double the other'; inverse means 'double one, halve the other.'

teach.caption: The line starts at $35, not at $0, so cost is linear but NOT directly proportional to miles.

items: Jasmine Patel books a wheelchair van for her grandmother: C = 2.5m + 35.
Slope 2.5 = rate of change: each extra mile adds $2.50. Intercept 35 = starting value: the $35 pickup fee charged even at 0 miles.
Direct? Test y ÷ x: 60 ÷ 10 = 6 but 85 ÷ 20 = 4.25. The ratio isn't constant, so it is NOT direct variation. Doubling the miles from 10 to 20 raises the cost from $60 to $85, not to $120.

teach.h: Worked example: slope from two points
items: Slope = rise ÷ run = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁). Use the van's points (10, 60) and (20, 85).
Rise: 85 − 60 = 25. Run: 20 − 10 = 10. Slope = 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5 dollars per mile. ✓ (matches the equation)
Intercept: start from one point and go back to x = 0: 60 − 2.5 × 10 = 60 − 25 = 35. ✓
Sign check: a positive slope rises left to right; a negative slope falls; a zero slope is horizontal.

teach.body: In direct variation, y = kx: the ratio y ÷ x is the same for every pair, and the graph is a straight line through the origin. A hospital aide paid $32 an hour has pay = 32 × hours: 5 hours earns $160, 10 hours earns $320. Find k from one pair (k = y ÷ x), then use it for any other x. If the line misses (0, 0), it is linear but not direct.

teach.h: Inverse: time to infuse 1,200 mL vs rate
teach.caption: Rate × time = 1,200 every time. Double the rate from 100 to 200 mL/h and the time halves from 12 to 6 hours.

items: Three volunteers take 8 hours to pack a clinic's supply kits. Total work = 3 × 8 = 24 volunteer-hours (the constant product).
With 4 volunteers working at the same pace: time = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 hours. Check: 4 × 6 = 24. ✓
MORE volunteers means FEWER hours. Setting it up as a direct proportion (3/8 = 4/x gives 10.7 hours) is the classic slip.

teach.text: Classic slips: calling the intercept the rate (or the slope the starting fee); computing slope as run over rise; calling y = 3x + 2 direct variation even though it misses the origin; and treating an inverse situation (more workers, fewer hours) as direct.

items: Linear y = mx + b: slope m = rate of change per 1 unit of x; intercept b = value when x = 0.
Slope = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁): rise over run.
Direct y = kx: constant ratio y ÷ x, line through the origin, double x → double y.
Inverse y = k/x: constant product xy, double x → halve y.

summary: You can now interpret slope as a rate and the intercept as a starting value, find a slope from two points, and tell direct, linear and inverse relationships apart from their equations, tables and graphs. You can also solve real-world problems with each type.

A.q: A gym membership costs C = 15m + 50 dollars for m months. What does the 50 represent?
options: The rate of change per month
A.why: In y = mx + b, b is the starting value: the cost when m = 0. So $50 is a one-time fee paid before any months are counted. The monthly charge is the slope, $15.

whyNot.0: The amount charged every month is the slope, $15, not the intercept.
whyNot.2: The rate of change per month is the slope, 15.

A.q: In which table does y vary directly with x?
A.why: Direct variation has a constant ratio y ÷ x: 7 ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 4 = 21 ÷ 6 = 3.5. So y = 3.5x.

whyNot.0: y rises by 2 each step, so it is linear, but 5 ÷ 2 ≠ 7 ÷ 4, so it is not direct (y = x + 3).
whyNot.1: x × y = 24 every time: this is inverse variation.
whyNot.3: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 but 16 ÷ 4 = 4: the ratio isn't constant (y = x²).

A.q: Six nurses take 4 hours to give flu shots to every employee at a company. Working at the same rate per nurse, how long would 8 nurses take to do the same job? Round to the nearest tenth.
A.why: This is inverse variation: total work = 6 × 4 = 24 nurse-hours. Time = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 hours. Check: 8 × 3 = 24.

whyNot.0: 2 hours takes one hour off for each extra nurse; the product 24 must stay constant, which gives 3.
whyNot.2: 5.3 hours sets it up as a direct proportion (4 × 8 ÷ 6), but more nurses need FEWER hours.
whyNot.3: 6 hours adds time for the extra nurses, but more nurses finish sooner.

B.q: A home-health agency reimburses a nurse $26 for a 40-mile week and $59 for a 100-mile week, following a linear rule. What is the reimbursement rate per mile?
B.why: Slope = change in pay ÷ change in miles = (59 − 26) ÷ (100 − 40) = 33 ÷ 60 = $0.55 per mile. (The rule is pay = 0.55m + 4.)

whyNot.1: $0.59 is 59 ÷ 100, which divides one total by one distance and ignores the $4 base amount.
whyNot.2: $0.65 is 26 ÷ 40, the same mistake using the first week.
whyNot.3: $1.82 is 60 ÷ 33, run over rise instead of rise over run.

B.q: Which equation shows a linear relationship that is NOT direct variation?
B.why: y = 4x + 3 is a straight line (constant rate 4) but starts at 3, not at the origin, so y ÷ x is not constant: linear but not direct.

whyNot.0: y = 2.5x passes through the origin with constant ratio 2.5: direct variation.
whyNot.1: y = 4/x + 3 has x in the denominator, so its graph is a curve, not a line.
whyNot.2: y = x/4 is the same as y = 0.25x, which is direct variation with k = 0.25.

B.q: The quantity y varies inversely with x. When x = 5, y = 12. What is y when x = 15?
B.why: Inverse variation: x × y = k = 5 × 12 = 60. When x = 15, y = 60 ÷ 15 = 4. Tripling x divides y by 3.

whyNot.1: 6 halves y, but x tripled, so y must be divided by 3.
whyNot.2: 22 adds the change in x (10) to y, which is neither direct nor inverse.
whyNot.3: 36 triples y, which is direct variation.

C.q: A medical supply courier charges a flat fee plus a constant rate per mile. A 12-mile delivery costs $41 and a 20-mile delivery costs $57. What does a 30-mile delivery cost?

whyNot.0: $73 adds $16 (the change for 8 miles) to $57, but going from 20 to 30 miles is 10 miles, or $20.
whyNot.2: $85.50 treats cost as directly proportional, scaling $57 by 30/20 and ignoring the flat fee.
whyNot.3: $102.50 scales $41 by 30/12, again treating a linear cost as direct variation.

C.q: A 1,000 mL IV bag would last 8 hours at 125 mL per hour. If the rate is changed to 200 mL per hour, how many hours will a full bag last?
C.why: Rate × time = 1,000 mL stays constant (inverse variation). Time = 1,000 ÷ 200 = 5 hours. Check: 200 × 5 = 1,000.

whyNot.0: 4 hours assumes the rate doubled; 200 is 1.6 times 125, not 2 times.
whyNot.2: The bag's volume is fixed, so a faster rate must shorten the time.
whyNot.3: 12.8 scales 8 hours up by 200/125, a direct proportion, but a faster rate means LESS time.

C.q: A table shows x: 0, 2, 4, 6 and y: 9, 15, 21, 27. Which describes the relationship?
C.why: y rises 6 for every 2 of x, so the slope is 6 ÷ 2 = 3. At x = 0, y = 9, so the intercept is 9: y = 3x + 9. Check: 3 × 6 + 9 = 27.

whyNot.0: At x = 0, y = 9, not 0, so the line misses the origin and is not direct variation.
whyNot.1: 6 is the rise per step of 2 in x; the slope divides by the run: 6 ÷ 2 = 3.
whyNot.3: This swaps the slope and the intercept.

reteach.title: Pizza for the night shift
reteach.question: You're ordering pizza for a night shift. How do the delivery fee, the price per pizza and splitting the bill show linear, direct and inverse relationships?

blocks.body: Pizzas cost $12 each with no fee: total = 12p, which is DIRECT (2 pizzas $24, 4 pizzas $48). Add a $5 delivery fee: total = 12p + 5, which is LINEAR but not direct (2 pizzas $29, 4 pizzas $53, not double). Now split a $60 order among the staff: each person pays 60 ÷ n, which is INVERSE (3 people pay $20 each, 6 people pay $10 each). Same pizza, three relationships.

blocks.text: The quick test: double x. If y doubles, it's direct. If y halves, it's inverse. If y changes by a constant step but doesn't double, it's linear with a starting value.

explain.body: In y = mx + b, the slope m is the change in y for each 1-unit increase in x (a rate), and b is the value of y when x = 0 (the starting amount). A negative slope means y decreases.

test.q: The equation y = −40x + 600 gives the milliliters y left in an IV bag after x hours. What does −40 mean?
test.why: −40 is the slope: each hour, y changes by −40, so the volume falls by 40 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: The starting volume is the intercept, 600 mL.
whyNot.1: The bag empties when y = 0: 600 ÷ 40 = 15 hours.
whyNot.2: The negative sign means the volume decreases, not increases.

explain.body: Slope = rise ÷ run = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁). Subtract in the same order on top and bottom, and always put the change in y on top.

test.q: A line passes through the points (2, 11) and (6, 23). What is its slope?

whyNot.2: 3.83 divides one y-value by one x-value (23 ÷ 6) instead of change by change.
whyNot.3: 5.5 divides 11 by 2, the coordinates of one point, instead of the changes.

explain.body: y = kx. Find k = y ÷ x from any known pair, then multiply by the new x. The graph passes through the origin, and doubling x doubles y.

head: Hours (x)
Pay (y)
y ÷ x
explain.caption: The ratio y ÷ x never changes. That constant is k.

test.q: The quantity y varies directly with x, and y = 18 when x = 4. What is y when x = 10?

whyNot.1: 24 adds the change in x (6) to y instead of multiplying by the constant ratio.
whyNot.3: 72 multiplies 18 by 4 instead of dividing to find k.

explain.body: y = k/x, so x × y = k stays constant. As x grows, y shrinks: double x and y halves; triple x and y is divided by 3.

test.q: The quantity y varies inversely with x. If x is doubled, what happens to y?
test.why: x × y must stay equal to k. If x doubles, y must halve to keep the product the same.

whyNot.1: y doubling with x is direct variation.
whyNot.2: Adding a fixed amount describes a linear change, not inverse variation.
whyNot.3: If y stayed the same, the product xy would double, but it must stay constant.
